items.title: [codex] Preserve disabled MCP servers across runtime overlays
preserve disabled MCP servers across runtime overlays

observed_change: Codex preserves configured `enabled = false` MCP servers after runtime fallback and extension overlays are applied.
user_visible_path: Users who explicitly disable an MCP server, including `codex_apps`, should not have that server re-enabled by compatibility or extension-provided runtime overlays.
control_plane_relevance: High for Decodex Control Plane because disabled MCP server intent is a core operator safety and compatibility boundary for plugin/app-server orchestration.
compatibility_risk: Medium positive compatibility fix: upstream now preserves disabled server state, so Decodex should stop assuming runtime overlays may override `enabled = false` on same-name servers once this version is present.
adoption_opportunity: Use this behavior as evidence that disabled MCP server state survives runtime overlays and simplify Decodex troubleshooting around unexpected `codex_apps` initialization.
community_value: High for MCP and app/plugin operators because it prevents explicitly disabled servers from being initialized by overlay defaults.
deprecated_or_breaking_notes: No MCP server is removed; the change restores disabled state after overlays while preserving `Remove` precedence and other overlay fields.
evidence: PR #27414 says same-name runtime overlays could default replacement MCP configs to enabled and initialize a server explicitly configured with `enabled = false`.
`codex-rs/core/src/mcp.rs` records disabled server names before adding runtime fallbacks and extension overlays.
`codex-rs/core/src/mcp.rs` restores `enabled = false` for those names after overlay application when the server remains present.
The PR body says the connection manager already filtered disabled servers, but the configured disabled state was lost before that filter.
The normalized bundle `artifacts/github/bundles/openai-codex-pr-27414.json` records 2 changed files for the merged PR.
caveats: The behavior is a targeted MCP runtime-overlay fix. It does not change unrelated MCP connection filtering or remove overlay fields.

next_actions.reason: Disabled MCP server preservation is directly relevant to Control Plane safety and compatibility.
The fix has a concise operator-facing explanation for MCP users.
Audit Decodex MCP troubleshooting notes for stale warnings about runtime overlays re-enabling disabled servers.
